html:
The law code of the Ming dynasty of China, issued in its final form in 1397 by the founding emperor, the Hongwu Emperor.

Hongwu, born a poor peasant, wanted a fixed, simple law that ordinary officials could apply and that would restore order after Mongol rule. The code was mainly criminal law. It listed crimes and their set punishments, from beatings with a stick to exile and death, and graded penalties by family relation and rank. Its articles were grouped by the six ministries of government. Earlier codes back to the Tang code were its models.

Hongwu forbade any change to it, so later emperors added rules in separate edicts. The code ruled China until 1644. The Qing took it over almost whole as the Great Qing Code, which lasted until 1912. Joseon Korea also applied it in criminal cases, which spread its reach beyond China.
sum: The law code of the Ming dynasty of China, issued in its final form in 1397 by the founding emperor, the Hongwu Emperor.
